approach: The velocity is parallel to the incline when its direction from the horizontal equals the incline angle; the constant horizontal component then fixes the speed directly.

steps.text: Write the constant horizontal component and the time-varying vertical component of velocity.
The velocity is parallel to the incline when its angle from the horizontal equals the incline's angle of 30°.
Solve for the time at which this holds.
At this angle, the horizontal component and the speed are related through the cosine of 30°, giving the speed directly.

common_mistakes.text: Swapping sine and cosine in the horizontal component of the launch velocity gives a wrong horizontal speed and a wrong final speed of exactly 40 m/s.
